process: Just-in-time cards from approved designs; each card runs the drift protocol and updates this index as if merged. Session execution and queued deployed acceptance follow docs/SESSION-START.md. Session PR counts are informational; combine related approved slices and checkpoint for context safety. Owner-requested throughput measurement: average 400–800 changed production-code lines and 2–5 fully completed slices per substantive PR; record actual diffs/slice evidence and use session:status for remaining indexed units. These are advisory averages, never padding or acceptance claims. Owner clarification 2026-10-14: PR workload accounting counts whole predefined batch subsections in the authoritative roadmap/design, never a function, UI hookup, guard, helper or execution-packet subtask. Partial subsections count zero completed batch subsections; count each subsection once with full eligible engineering and pre-merge evidence. Group related subsections into substantial PRs; use focused checks during work and full required gates on the coherent PR. Existing acceptance and safety gates remain.

revisit.reason: Audit finding VMCP-001 (docs/MCP-AUDIT-2026-10-27.md, P0): the executor demands a one-use separately-authenticated purchase grant for every paid write and refuses recurring or unquantified spend outright. Owner ruling OP-2 (2026-10-27) replaces that product-scope wall with a standing owner policy: an optional owner-set agent budget plus an optional grant-required opt-in; the owner's word executes and is journaled. Design D-A is filed as a BATCH-B amendment (2026-10-27); remediation issues #108-#110, #116 and #119 describe the same mandatory grant shape for end users. VMCP-020 (return the effective request key in applied write results, plus stable-key guidance) rides the same executor seam as a separate PR under the BATCH-B amendment note.

Separately, per the BATCH-B VMCP-020 note: return the effective request key in every applied write result and add stable-key guidance where request keys are introduced; do not fold that change into AUD-A2's risk boundary.

For VMCP-020, a captured applied write result showing the effective request key.
revisit.eligibilityCondition: Eligible now; OP-2 ruled 2026-10-27 and no further owner input is needed.
revisit.resolution: AUD-A1 leg implemented (audit pipeline S6, 2026-10-28): vercel_accounts gains purchase_budget_cents (nullable; NULL = no budget) and purchase_grant_required (BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT FALSE), additively; a durable one-row marker in the new schema_migrations table gates the one-time carry of a positive spend_limit_cents into purchase_budget_cents (marker insert and carry are one statement, so a budget the owner later clears is never resurrected by the per-request initSchema); db.getPurchasePolicy/setPurchasePolicy sit beside setOwnerSpendLimit with read-back verification and a journaled vercel_set_purchase_policy change_log row per set; the setup page gains a Purchase policy section on the existing owner seam (sibling set_purchase_policy action, production-only, confirm + fresh passphrase) whose re-rendered page reads the stored policy back; vercel_whoami reports purchaseBudgetCents and purchaseGrantRequired beside the existing spend fields. spend_limit_cents is NOT dropped and no executor file changed — the executor stays grant-bound until AUD-A2, which remains this revisit's open leg (plus the separate VMCP-020 PR). VMCP-001 closes only at S7 live verification after AUD-A2. AUD-A2 leg implemented (audit pipeline S6, 2026-10-28): write-preflight now classifies the connection from the server-minted kind on the door-minted context (owner's own connector/OAuth connection = owner; pass, builder and unclassified connections fail closed to the grant path — never a caller argument). On an owner connection whose stored policy has purchase_grant_required false, the preflight evaluates getPurchasePolicy/getTodaySpendCents, frames the confirmed cost against the budget ('today so far' for the account's America/Denver day), and carries a purchase.delegation block instead of the grant check: fixed-price quotes disclose the dollar line and budget state, quotedCents is null for metered or zero-priced recurring charges (cost depends on usage — the former blanket refusal and the Sandbox special case are gone on this path), and over-budget executes with overBudget true because the owner's word overrides their own budget (OP-2). The executor runs on confirm alone, creates and consumes no purchase intent on this path, hands tools a frozen purchaseDelegation context (via purchaseDelegationFor), keeps the pre-dispatch price re-check, and journals the delegation block into change_log.result.delegation through recordChange (validated, credential-scanned); grant-required owners, delegates and builders keep the existing grant flow byte-for-byte, including consumed approvals and the Sandbox exception wording re-scoped to that path. The two retired-rule comments in src/core/write.js are re-scoped to delegated/builder connections, citing docs/END-USER-AUTHORITY.md. This revisit's evidence is met on fakes (owner confirm-only apply with no intent, over-budget journaling, delegate unchanged, builder regression green); VMCP-020 remains a separate PR, and VMCP-001 — with issues #108-#110, #116 and #119, explicitly carried — closes only at S7 live verification.

revisit.reason: Audit findings VMCP-011, VMCP-008 and VMCP-010 (docs/MCP-AUDIT-2026-10-27.md) all break this card's stored-overflow promise on one side or another: an oversized guarded write throws after the provider write has landed because the stored fallback exists only on the read branch of src/vercel/result-delivery.js; the write-preflight safeShape throw turns the 8 KB ceiling into a refusal of the whole change; and the globalconfig family self-shapes past the fallback in src/tools/globalconfig-common.js. Design D-D is filed as a BATCH-C amendment (2026-10-27): symmetry - the stored-result contract applies to writes, previews and every tool family.
revisit.checkpoint: At the AUD-D PR boundary; sequence after packet AUD-A2 because both edit src/core/write-preflight.js.
revisit.nextAction: Implement packet docs/pr-cards/AUD-D.md: the write branch of shapeMcpResult gains the stored fallback returning the verified receipt plus a res_ handle; oversized previews store and reference instead of refusing (secret-bearing previews still refuse); self-shaped families route through the shared delivery path, proven by a repo-wide grep recorded in the PR.
revisit.evidenceNeeded: AUD-D acceptance evidence: the audit's three executed probes reproduced as tests - oversized write returning receipt plus handle with vercel_get_result serving the full result; oversized preview completing with a stored reference; a globalconfig oversized output returning the same stored-handle contract.
revisit.eligibilityCondition: Eligible now; no owner input needed. Sequencing after AUD-A2 is a file-contention rule, not an owner gate.
revisit.resolution: Implemented (audit pipeline S6, packet AUD-D, 2026-10-28): the write branch of shapeStoredMcpResult (src/vercel/result-delivery.js) now mirrors the read branch — an oversized write result is stored through db.putResult under the same connection-scoped rules and the caller receives the write's own verified receipt (status, confirmed, mode, requestKey — the change-log lookup key — plus a small target summary when it fits) with a resultHandle res_ handle and a note naming vercel_get_result; if storage is unavailable the answer is the executor's outcome_unknown honesty shape, never a throw after dispatch. In src/core/write-preflight.js a new safeShapeStored distinguishes cannot-shape-safely (shaper throws for a non-size reason — unchanged refusal) from shaped-but-large: the preview in writePreflight and the target list in the executor's audit base are stored and referenced by the read path's stored-receipt shape, so the write proceeds to confirmation; with no usable result store the oversized case keeps the original refusal (no truncation, no raised cap). The globalconfig family's output() and its two nested compact() shapes (safeItems values, the schema definition) now redact at the result store's 1 MB cap and let the shared delivery path decide inline vs stored; inline-sized output is byte-identical, and the remaining direct compact() shapes in src/tools are the guarded-write output functions over executor results already bounded by safeShape (justified in the AUD-D PR). The executor's verify/read-back and the replay result bound are untouched. Evidence: the audit's three executed probes reproduced as tests (oversized write receipt + handle with vercel_get_result paging the stored result for the same bearer only and refusing another; oversized preview and target list completing with stored references while an unshapable preview still refuses; an oversized globalconfig output returning the stored contract). VMCP-008, VMCP-010 and VMCP-011 close only at S7 live verification.

Audit finding VMCP-022 (2026-10-28, P1) lands on this card's enrollment seam: probeToken in src/vercel/tokens.js requires user_get, teams_list and projects_list reads from a newly enrolled token (teamId attached) and refuses to save unless the team is visible in teams_list, which a genuinely project-scoped token cannot satisfy per Vercel's scoped-token documentation (scope inferred; teamId applies to full-account tokens only). Live evidence: the IN-06 rtc-scratch token, verified in Vercel's own list, failed setup enrollment twice on 2026-10-28 with the generic catch-all failure, which also hides which probe leg failed (the D10 aspect).
revisit.resolution: Owner ruling recorded in docs/OWNER-INPUTS.md (IN-04) and docs/DECISIONS.md on 2026-10-27: the server respects the expiry the owner chose and its only duty is to notify ahead of an upcoming expiration (14 days before) for keys that have one. Enrolled-token leg implemented by packet AUD-E (audit pipeline S6, 2026-10-28): vercel_accounts gains token_no_expiry (BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT FALSE, additive); the owner-only setup attestation (sibling set_token_no_expiry action, production-only, confirm + fresh passphrase, journaled vercel_set_token_no_expiry change_log rows with read-back) is the establishment bridge until the O-3 token tools record the choice at creation, and enrolling or rotating a token clears any prior attestation. A shared derivation (src/vercel/token-expiry.js) drives both surfaces in packet order — stored past date expired, stored future date expiring, null date + attestation no_expiry, null date unattested unknown ('expiry not recorded for this token', never owner's choice): vercel_whoami returns expiresAt/expiresAtLocal/daysLeft/expiryPosture/expiryPostureText with tokenWarning byte-compatible, and the setup account list states the posture per account with a banner only inside the 14-day window or once expired. VMCP-003's token-tool leg (creation-time recording of the owner's choice) remains this card's scope; VMCP-003 closes only at S7 live verification.
